metaDescription: Pug vaccine schedule with core ages in weeks. Set reminders so Pug boosters are not missed.

bodySections.heading: Why timing matters for this schedule
paragraphs: Why timing is non-negotiable for Pugs: each booster lands after the previous dose’s immunology window, usually every 2–4 weeks, until the Pug series closes at about 16 weeks.
Size class small does not invent new viruses for the Pug, but it does change crate fit, blood-draw ease, and how early you lock travel relative to the final DA2PP / DHPP booster.
Flag obesity at Pug vaccine checkups so the puppy’s chart accumulates breed-relevant context, not just sticker dates.
When the Pug series is complete, switch reminders to adult booster cadence instead of deleting the vaccine thread entirely.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: Owners postpone Pug shots when the puppy seems “a little off,” travel intervenes, or brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (boas) worries dominate the week — ask the clinic whether a same-week Pug make-up is still appropriate instead of sliding to the annual exam.
Long gaps can leave Pug antibody levels uncertain, so expect either an added booster or a titer conversation rather than a shrug.
Do not trade the missed Pug dose for extra socialization; finish immunity first for this small dog.
Reset the Pug reminder stack the evening of the make-up appointment — including the eventual adult booster after the 16-week finish.

faqs.question: When does the Pug core vaccine series usually finish?
faqs.answer: This breed record completes core vaccines around 16 weeks of age, with rabies timed per local law. Your clinic may adjust intervals for the individual puppy.

faqs.question: What should I do if my Pug misses a booster?
faqs.answer: Contact your veterinarian for a catch-up plan instead of restarting or skipping ahead. Keep prior dates handy and limit high-risk exposure until the series is current again.

faqs.question: Where can I read Pug health context beyond vaccines?
faqs.answer: See the Pug adult health guide for breed predispositions such as brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (boas), then bring those notes to wellness and vaccine visits.
